ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RELEASE POLICIES

Blanchard Terminal Company LLC - Selma Buffalo Terminal (Selma Buffalo) is a refined petroleum products terminal distributing refined product throughout the Selma, NC region including various grades of gasoline and distillates.   The RMP-regulated process/stationary source is limited to the Butane Blending Process inclusive of a single truck offload station, two pressure vessels, a pump, piping and various appurtenances.  

The Terminal is committed to operating and maintaining its processes in a safe, reliable and environmentally sound manner. Selma Buffalo believes that excellent performance in health, environmental, and safety (HES) goes hand-in-hand with operating reliability.

Selma Buffalo is designed, operated, and maintained in a manner that promotes the health and safety of its workers, contractors, and the community along with protecting the environment. This is accomplished through programs of awareness, compliance, prevention and mitigation. These programs include a combination of accidental release prevention and emergency response planning. This document provides a brief overview of the comprehensive risk management activities including:

A. A description of the facility and the use of regulated substances (n-Butane);
B. An overview of the accidental release prevention program (Program Level 3);
C. A five-year accident history for accidental releases of RMP-regulated chemicals;
D. An overview of the emergency response program; and
E. An overview of planned changes to improve safety.

A. STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES

The Butane Blending Process has been classified as Prevention Program Level 3. No Program 1 or 2 processes are identified at the facility. By virtue of the flammable effects associated with butane, it is necessary to observe certain safety precautions to prevent unnecessary human exposure, reduce the threat to employee health, and minimize the threat and impact to n

earby members of the community.  Safety at the Facility depends upon the manner in which butane is handled as well as the various safety devices/systems incorporated into the design of the Butane Blending Process. Furthermore, comprehensive training is provided to employees which reinforces the safety policies and procedures of the Terminal.

The facility maintains fixed inventories of Butane. Butane is received by truck (transports) and stored in two (2) pressurized storage vessels.  The butane is pumped to a blending skid for direct injection into blend-grade and premium unleaded gasoline lines feeding the site gasoline truck-loading rack. Injection quantities are controlled via the blending skid control valves and dedicated Gasoline Analyzer. Process safety controls include excess flow valves, fusible elements (<250 degrees Fahrenheit), pneumatic valves (fail safe), 85% fill shutoff on the vessel, emergency shut-off devices throughout the system (including the video display terminal, piping hydrostatic reliefs, vessel multiport pressure reliefs, and grounding/interlock devices. The process is remotely monitored "24/7".  Access to the Terminal is restricted to authorized employees, management personnel and authorized contractors/visitors.

B. GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION MEASURES

The Selma Buffalo accidental release prevention programs and emergency planning/response programs help effectively manage the hazards posed by regulated substances to its employees, the public, and the environment. The covered process is regulated by the EPA RMP regulation 40 CFR Part 68, as well as the OSHA Process Safety Management standard 29CFR 1910.119. The following accident prevention program elements are in place at Selma Buffalo Terminal:

1) Employee Participation,
2) Process Safety Information,
3) Process Hazard Analysis (PHA),
4) Standard Operating Procedures,
5) Operator and Maintenance Personnel Training
6) Contractor Manage

at key process areas to warn of a Butane release and disable all Terminal process;
-Fire monitors installed near offload area; and 
-An intumescent coating on vessels.

General Emergency Response:

-Emergency alert system,
-Periodic emergency training for employees,
-Communication systems with local emergency responders and regulatory agencies,
-Emergency drills/exercises with terminal personnel, regulatory agencies, and community emergency responders to enhance response skills and coordination among agencies,
-Mutual Aid with Local Fire Departments.

Further, the Terminal complies with NFPA's Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Code (NFPA-58) requirements for LP Gas storage. In addition to the presence of appropriate release prevention controls, a Facility Response Plan (FRP) [aka "SMART PLAN"] is in place with the facility and response activities being coordinated with Selma Fire Department and the Johnston County LECP.

C. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

Selma Buffalo has an excellent record of accident prevention. The Terminal maintains records for all chemical releases that occur within the facility. There have been no reportable accidents within the past five (5) years resulting from the release of materials covered under the EPA RMP regulation.

D. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

A Facility Response Plan/"SMART PLAN" is in place to inform employees what to do in case of a release and/or fire, and to notify community emergency responders when there is a need for a response.  

The Terminal maintains a relationship with the Selma Fire Department and Johnston County LEPC. Tours, training and drills/exercises with members of local emergency response organizations are held annually, at a minimum. These events enable the public emergency responders to become familiar with Butane hazards, equipment, resources and personnel in the Terminal.

E. PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY

The Terminal is continually reviewing current alarms to determine if any may not be critical to the pr

ocess to avoid potential operator complacency.  All Process Safety Events (as defined in API 754) are electronically recorded, reviewed, and investigated.  The investigation may include a root-cause analysis (ex. TapRooT) per corporate policy depending on the nature and/or severity of the incident.   The Terminal and Corporate stakeholders maintain continuous lines of communication with its business partner to identify areas of process improvement.
